name: Grey willow
note: Grey willow, Salix cinerea (docs 10, 14): the island's first shrub, a many-stemmed bush of wet, fresh banks. Drawn with the shrub shader (draw: shrub; src/shaders/flora-shrub.wgsl), which gorse can share later with other numbers. habitat, growth, flowering, dormant, spread and starter work as in reeds.json: willow wants a moist bank on soil near fresh water (moisture falls to nothing within 3 m of fresh water, so the moisture axis keeps it close; salt keeps it off the shore), at most a few centimeters of standing water, and gentle slopes. It grows slowly, over about a game season to full size, and size reveals it: height and crown grow with it. It is not a starter (recipes/world/growth.json): it arrives by itself after marsh marigold (starter is used only by ?plants=all and a basin's own starters). New fields. spread.window: season positions (0 spring .. 4) when a mature shrub may drop seed (willow's fluffy seed flies in early summer); outside it no seed falls. spread.maxCount: no more seed takes once the island holds this many of the species, and with minSpacingM it keeps a bank from becoming a willow wall (the Plant tool may still plant more). phenology: leafOut and leafFall are the season windows over which the leaves come out and fall (without them a shrub is evergreen); maleShare is the share of shrubs that are male (willows are male or female: male catkins ripen yellow with pollen, female ones green). Shape (flora-shrub.wgsl): stemsPerShrub stems (more as it grows) rise from a stool of clumpRadius (also the cover frogs hide in, src/world/creatures/day-hide.js), leaning out so their tips reach leanShare of the crown radius, crownRadius x size, the shrub maxHeight x size tall (varied by heightVar, never under sproutM); stems are stemWidth wide at the base, tapering to twigWidth, arching outward by arch (share of height); each forks forks[0] to forks[1] times (more as it grows) between forkAt[0] and [1] of its length, forkDeg off it. Toward the tips of each stem and fork sit cardsPerBranch cards of cardM: sprays drawn as a twig and two twiglets carrying leaves on a leafGrid x leafGrid jittered grid (each leafM long, leafWidth of its length wide) or, while flowering, catkinsPerCard catkins of catkinM. season: albedo of the leaves (linear) per season (the autumn turn comes from it), of the bark, the young red-brown twigs, the catkins as they open (silver) and ripe (pollen yellow on males, green on females). wind: stiffness keeps the stems stiff, sway is their tip bend per unit wind (share of height), flutter turns the leaf sprays. look: rootShade at the foot, innerShade toward the crown's middle (the crown is lit as one mass with an ellipsoid's normal at crownMiddle of the height), undersideShare of leaves show their pale undersides, wetDarken in rain, pixelWidth keeps far stems and twigs at least that wide. contactShadow: a soft disc on the ground under each shrub, radiusShare of the crown radius, darkening by strength at the stool (bareShare of that while bare), its rim drawn out away from the sun by sunShift of the height, liftM above the ground, in layers stacked layerM apart (each a share of the darkening, so the grass under the bush darkens down its blades); flora casts no real shadows until the trees in M4.

phenology.jitterNote: each plant keeps its own calendar, offset from the species by up to jitterDays game days either way (hash of the plant id; src/world/growth/phenology.js), so its flowering, seeding and dormant windows (and the willow's leaf-out and leaf fall) do not all turn on the same hour
